%7C%202000%20%7C%2031.30%20%7C%0A%20%20%20%20%7C%202001%20%7C%2032.80%20%7C%0A%20%20%20%20%7C%202002%20%7C%2032.00%20%7C%0A%20%20%20%20%7C%202003%20to%202004%20%7C%2033.60%20%7C%0A%20%20%20%20%7C%202005%20to%202006%20%7C%2035.00%20%7C%0A%20%20%20%20%7C%202007%20to%202008%20%7C%2036.00%20%7C%0A%20%20%20%20%7C%202009%20to%202010%20%7C%2038.00%20%7C%0A%20%20%20%20%7C%202011%20to%202012%20%7C%2039.00%20%7C%0A%20%20%20%20%7C%202013%20%7C%2041.00%20%7C%0A%0A%20%20%20%20-%20From%202003%20on%2C%20the%20amount%20rises%20**every%20two%20years%20by%20about%203%20to%206%20%25**%2C%20in%20line%20with%20an%20adjustment%20for%20inflation.%0A%20%20%20%20-%20The%20only%20decrease%20is%20from%2032.80%20to%2032.00%20in%202002%2C%20the%20year%20in%20which%20the%20euro%20cash%20was%20introduced.%20*Question%3A*%20Is%20this%20a%20result%20of%20the%20conversion%3F%0A%20%20%20%20-%20The%20old%20amount%20is%20used%20for%20only%20a%20few%20days%20into%20the%20new%20year%20(for%20example%2033.60%20until%2009.01.2005).%20This%20suggests%20that%20the%20date%20of%20the%20offence%20decides%20on%20the%20amount%2C%20and%20that%20some%20fines%20are%20entered%20with%20a%20short%20delay.%0A%20%20%20%20-%20Two%20single%20cases%20have%20about%20double%20the%20amount%20(65.60%20in%202001%20and%2071.00%20in%202005).%20They%20are%20probably%20errors%20or%20special%20cases.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20*Finding%3A*%20Comparing%20amounts%20over%20the%20years%2C%20as%20in%20Task%202.5%2C%20should%20take%20this%20drift%20into%20account.%20An%20interactive%20menu%20is%20included%20above%2C%20so%20other%20articles%20can%20be%20studied%20in%20the%20same%20way.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Task%205.7%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Task%205.7%20-%20Hypothesis%0A%0A%20%20%20%20If%20the%20sharp%20drop%20of%20Task%205.4c%20comes%20from%20a%20legal%20deadline%20that%20existed%20for%20the%20whole%20log%2C%20the%20distribution%20for%20cases%20that%20start%20after%201%20September%202010%20should%20keep%20the%20same%20shape.%20The%20date%20in%20the%20task%20suggests%20that%20something%20changes%20around%20then%2C%20so%20we%20expect%20a%20different%20distribution%3A%20possibly%20a%20shift%20of%20the%20peak%20or%20a%20different%20limit.%20Fines%20of%20the%20last%20months%20have%20had%20less%20time%20to%20be%20sent%2C%20but%20this%20should%20matter%20little%2C%20because%20the%20log%20runs%20for%20almost%20three%20more%20years.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(case_log_s5%2C%20day_chart%2C%20delay_days%2C%20mo%2C%20pd)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_all%20%3D%20delay_days('Create%20Fine'%2C%20'Send%20Fine')%0A%20%20%20%20_recent%20%3D%20_all%5B_all.index.isin(case_log_s5.index%5Bcase_log_s5%5B'start'%5D%20%3E%20pd.Timestamp('2010-09-01')%5D)%5D%0A%0A%20%20%20%20_groups%20%3D%20%7B'full%20log'%3A%20_all%2C%20'cases%20starting%20after%201%20Sept%202010'%3A%20_recent%7D%0A%20%20%20%20_summary%20%3D%20pd.DataFrame(%7B%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_name%3A%20_days.describe(percentiles%3D%5B0.1%2C%200.25%2C%200.5%2C%200.75%2C%200.9%2C%200.99%5D)%20for%20_name%2C%20_days%20in%20_groups.items()%0A%20%20%20%20%7D).round(1)%0A%20%20%20%20_summary.loc%5B'most%20frequent%20delay'%5D%20%3D%20%5B_d.value_counts().idxmax()%20for%20_d%20in%20_groups.values()%5D%0A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.vstack(%5B%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_summary%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20day_chart(_recent%2C%20'Create%20Fine%20%3E%20Send%20Fine%2C%20cases%20starting%20after%201%20Sept%202010%2C%20first%20400%20days'%2C%20max_days%3D400)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20day_chart(_all%2C%20'Create%20Fine%20%3E%20Send%20Fine%2C%20full%20log%2C%20first%20400%20days'%2C%20max_days%3D400)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Task%205.7%20-%20Result%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%7C%20Create%20Fine%20%3E%20Send%20Fine%20%7C%20Full%20log%20%7C%20Starting%20after%201%20Sept%202010%20%7C%0A%20%20%20%20%7C---%7C---%7C---%7C%0A%20%20%20%20%7C%20Cases%20%7C%20103'987%20%7C%2010'721%20%7C%0A%20%20%20%20%7C%20Median%20%7C%2088%20days%20%7C%2050%20days%20%7C%0A%20%20%20%20%7C%20Mean%20%7C%2087.5%20days%20%7C%2054.8%20days%20%7C%0A%20%20%20%20%7C%2075th%20percentile%20%7C%20121%20days%20%7C%2059%20days%20%7C%0A%20%20%20%20%7C%2090th%20percentile%20%7C%20136%20days%20%7C%2090%20days%20%7C%0A%20%20%20%20%7C%20Within%2060%20days%20%7C%2031.6%20%25%20%7C%2076.7%20%25%20%7C%0A%20%20%20%20%7C%20Within%2090%20days%20%7C%2052.1%20%25%20%7C%2090.3%20%25%20%7C%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**The%20distribution%20changes%20clearly.**%20The%20second%20hump%20around%20130%20days%20has%20disappeared%2C%20and%20there%20is%20only%20one%20peak%20around%2048%20to%2054%20days.%20The%20hard%20limit%20at%20150%20days%20has%20been%20replaced%20by%20a%20clear%20drop%20at%20about%2060%20days%3A%20from%20267%20cases%20on%20day%2059%20to%20170%20on%20day%2060%2C%20to%20115%20on%20day%2061.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Interpretation.**%20This%20fits%20the%20change%20of%20article%20201%20by%20the%20law%20120%2F2010%2C%20which%20shortened%20the%20deadline%20from%20150%20to%2090%20days%20(%5Bedotto%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fedotto.com%2Farticolo%2Fnotifica-pi-breve-per-le-multe)).%20So%20the%20150%20days%20of%20Task%205.4c%20only%20apply%20to%20the%20time%20before%20this%20change%2C%20and%20the%20full%20log%20mixes%20two%20regimes.%20The%20drop%20lies%20at%2060%20days%20instead%20of%2090.%20A%20possible%20reason%20is%20that%20the%20police%20keeps%20a%20margin%20of%20up%20to%2030%20days%20for%20the%20transit%20of%20the%20letter%2C%20so%20that%20the%20notification%20also%20arrives%20within%20the%2090%20days.%20Before%20the%20change%2C%20however%2C%20the%20police%20used%20the%20full%20150%20days%20(Task%205.4c)%2C%20so%20the%20log%20cannot%20confirm%20this%20reason.%20This%20shows%20why%20concept%20drift%20matters%3A%20a%20single%20distribution%20for%20the%20full%20log%20would%20hide%20the%20change.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20About%2010%20%25%20of%20the%20cases%20are%20still%20later%20than%2090%20days.%20These%20could%20be%20letters%20abroad%20or%20cases%20whose%20owner%20had%20to%20be%20identified%20first.%20The%20source%20does%20not%20tell%20us%20the%20exact%20date%20from%20which%20the%20new%20rule%20applied%2C%20so%20the%20date%20of%201%20September%20comes%20from%20the%20task.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(ACTIVITY%2C%20case_log_s5%2C%20mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20def%20has_activity(activity)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%23%20does%20the%20case%20contain%20the%20activity%20at%20least%20once%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20return%20case_log_s5%5B'seq_variant'%5D.apply(lambda%20variant%3A%20activity%20in%20variant)%0A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20def%20rule_report(applicable%2C%20violating)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%23%20the%20numbers%20that%20Task%206.1%20asks%20for%3B%20both%20arguments%20are%20numbers%20of%20cases%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_kept%20%3D%20applicable%20-%20violating%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20return%20mo.md(f%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20-%20Cases%20to%20which%20the%20constraint%20applies%3A%20**%7Bnum(applicable)%7D**%20of%20%7Bnum(len(case_log_s5))%7D%0A%20%20%20%20-%20**Violating%20cases%3A%20%7Bnum(violating)%7D**%20(%7Bviolating%20%2F%20applicable%3A.2%25%7D%20of%20the%20applicable%20cases)%0A%20%20%20%20-%20Precision%20of%20%22if%20...%20then%20...%22%3A%20**%7B_kept%20%2F%20applicable%3A.4f%7D**%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20RULE_COLUMNS%20%3D%20%5BACTIVITY%2C%20'amount'%2C%20'expense'%2C%20'paymentAmount'%2C%20'dismissal'%2C%20'notificationType'%2C%20'outstanding_amount'%5D%0A%20%20%20%20return%20RULE_COLUMNS%2C%20has_activity%2C%20rule_report%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20Session%206%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Task%206.1%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Task%206.1a%20-%20Hypothesis%0A%0A%20%20%20%20*Whenever%20a%20case%20has%20Insert%20Fine%20Notification%20then%20also%20Add%20penalty%20is%20present.*%20Task%204.2a%20already%20showed%20that%20both%20activities%20occur%20in%20the%20same%2079'860%20cases%2C%20so%20we%20expect%20**no%20violation**.%20This%20is%20surprising%20from%20a%20business%20point%20of%20view%2C%20because%20an%20offender%20who%20pays%20in%20time%20should%20not%20get%20a%20penalty.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(RULE_COLUMNS%2C%20event_log_s5%2C%20has_activity%2C%20mo%2C%20rule_report%2C%20show_case)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_notified%20%3D%20has_activity('Insert%20Fine%20Notification')%0A%20%20%20%20_violating%20%3D%20_notified%20%26%20~has_activity('Add%20penalty')%0A%20%20%20%20_violating_ids%20%3D%20_violating%5B_violating%5D.index%0A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.vstack(%5B%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20rule_report(int(_notified.sum())%2C%20int(_violating.sum()))%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20mo.md(f%22**Violating%20case%20%7B_violating_ids%5B0%5D%7D**%22)%20if%20len(_violating_ids)%20else%20mo.md(%22There%20is%20no%20violating%20case.%22)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20show_case(event_log_s5%2C%20_violating_ids%5B0%5D%2C%20RULE_COLUMNS)%20if%20len(_violating_ids)%20else%20mo.md(%22%22)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Task%206.1a%20-%20Result%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**0%20of%20the%2079'860%20applicable%20cases%20violate%20the%20constraint**%2C%20so%20it%20is%20valid%2C%20as%20expected.%20There%20is%20therefore%20no%20violating%20case%20to%20inspect.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Reflection.**%20The%20perfect%20result%20is%20itself%20suspicious.%20From%20a%20business%20point%20of%20view%20a%20fine%20that%20is%20notified%20and%20then%20paid%20in%20time%20should%20not%20get%20a%20penalty.%20Yet%20in%20this%20log%20such%20a%20fine%20does%20not%20exist.%20Together%20with%20Task%206.2%20this%20suggests%20that%20*Insert%20Fine%20Notification*%20is%20not%20recorded%20when%20the%20letter%20arrives%2C%20but%20only%20when%20a%20fine%20is%20still%20unpaid%20at%20the%20end%20of%20the%2060%20days%2C%20together%20with%20the%20penalty.%20An%20offender%20who%20pays%20in%20time%20would%20then%20have%20no%20notification%20in%20the%20log%20at%20all%2C%20as%20in%20the%20variant%20*Create%20Fine%20%3E%20Send%20Fine%20%3E%20Payment*.%20*Recommendation%20data%20collection%3A*%20Record%20each%20notification%20when%20it%20happens.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Task%206.1b%20-%20Hypothesis%0A%0A%20%20%20%20*Send%20Appeal%20to%20Prefecture%20is%20always%20eventually%20followed%20by%20Receive%20Result%20Appeal%20from%20Prefecture.*%20The%20table%20in%20Task%205.1%20shows%204'141%20cases%20with%20*Send%20Appeal%20to%20Prefecture*%20but%20only%20999%20with%20*Receive%20Result%20Appeal%20from%20Prefecture*%2C%20so%20we%20expect%20**at%20least%20about%203'100%20violations**%2C%20roughly%20three%20quarters%20of%20the%20appeals.%20Part%20of%20them%20could%20be%20appeals%20still%20running%20at%20the%20end%20of%20the%20log%2C%20but%20most%20should%20be%20results%20that%20were%20not%20recorded.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(%0A%20%20%20%20RULE_COLUMNS%2C%0A%20%20%20%20case_log_s5%2C%0A%20%20%20%20event_log_s5%2C%0A%20%20%20%20first_time%2C%0A%20%20%20%20has_activity%2C%0A%20%20%20%20mo%2C%0A%20%20%20%20pd%2C%0A%20%20%20%20rule_report%2C%0A%20%20%20%20show_case%2C%0A)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_send%2C%20_receive%20%3D%20'Send%20Appeal%20to%20Prefecture'%2C%20'Receive%20Result%20Appeal%20from%20Prefecture'%0A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20def%20_violates(variant)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_positions%20%3D%20%5B_i%20for%20_i%2C%20_a%20in%20enumerate(variant)%20if%20_a%20%3D%3D%20_send%5D%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20return%20any(_receive%20not%20in%20variant%5B_i%20%2B%201%3A%5D%20for%20_i%20in%20_positions)%0A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20_applicable%20%3D%20has_activity(_send)%0A%20%20%20%20_violating%20%3D%20case_log_s5.loc%5B_applicable%2C%20'seq_variant'%5D.apply(_violates)%0A%20%20%20%20_violating_ids%20%3D% 80%20in%202007).%20In%203'144%20of%20the%20violating%20cases%20*Send%20Appeal%20to%20Prefecture*%20is%20the%20very%20last%20event.%20So%20in%20most%20cases%20the%20process%20leaves%20the%20log%20at%20this%20point%2C%20and%20it%20is%20unclear%20whether%20the%20prefecture%20ever%20answered.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Case%20A10001.**%20The%20fine%20of%2036%20is%20notified%20on%2025.07.2007%2C%20and%20the%20appeal%20is%20entered%20on%2002.08.2007.%20The%20penalty%20is%20added%20on%2023.09.2007%2C%20and%20the%20appeal%20is%20sent%20on%2024.09.2007.%20On%20this%20last%20event%20%60dismissal%60%20changes%20to%20**%23**%2C%20which%20means%20dismissed%20by%20the%20prefecture%2C%20although%20no%20result%20was%20received.%20*Interpretation%3A*%20The%20result%20seems%20to%20be%20stored%20as%20the%20code%20on%20the%20sending%20event%2C%20instead%20of%20as%20a%20separate%20event.%20This%20cannot%20explain%20all%20of%20the%20violations%2C%20since%20Task%203.1%20found%20only%202'073%20dismissed%20cases%20in%20the%20whole%20log.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20*Questions%3A*%20How%20many%20of%20the%20violating%20cases%20have%20this%20code%3F%20What%20happened%20to%20the%20others%3F%20*Recommendation%20data%20collection%3A*%20Always%20record%20the%20result%20of%20an%20appeal%20as%20an%20event%20with%20its%20date.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Task%206.1c%20-%20Hypothesis%0A%0A%20%20%20%20*If%20Send%20Fine%20is%20on%20the%20same%20day%20as%20Create%20Fine%2C%20so%20is%20Insert%20Fine%20Notification.*%20In%20the%20few%20cases%20we%20have%20seen%20with%20this%20pattern%20(C20817%20and%20C10852%20in%20Task%205.1)%20all%20three%20events%20fall%20on%20one%20day%2C%20which%20suggests%20a%20fine%20that%20is%20handed%20over%20directly.%20So%20we%20expect%20the%20constraint%20to%20hold%20with%20**very%20few%20violations**.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(%0A%20%20%20%20RULE_COLUMNS%2C%0A%20%20%20%20case_log_s5%2C%0A%20%20%20%20event_log_s5%2C%0A%20%20%20%20first_time%2C%0A%20%20%20%20mo%2C%0A%20%20%20%20rule_report%2C%0A%20%20%20%20show_case%2C%0A)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_created%20%3D%20first_time('Create%20Fine').dt.normalize()%0A%20%20%20%20_sent%20%3D%20first_time('Send%20Fine').dt.normalize().reindex(case_log_s5.index)%0A%20%20%20%20_notified%20%3D%20first_time('Insert%20Fine%20Notification').dt.normalize().reindex(case_log_s5.index)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20_applicable%20%3D%20_sent%20%3D%3D%20_created.reindex(case_log_s5.index)%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20a%20missing%20notification%20counts%20as%20a%20violation%3A%20it%20is%20not%20on%20the%20same%20day%0A%20%20%20%20_violating%20%3D%20_applicable%20%26%20(_notified%20!%3D%20_created.reindex(case_log_s5.index))%0A%20%20%20%20_violating_ids%20%3D%20_violating%5B_violating%5D.index%0A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.vstack(%5B%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20rule_report(int(_applicable.sum())%2C%20int(_violating.sum()))%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20mo.md(f%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20-%20Violating%20cases%20without%20any%20*Insert%20Fine%20Notification*%3A%20**%7Bnum(_notified%5B_violating%5D.isna().sum())%7D**%0A%20%20%20%20-%20Violating%20cases%20with%20a%20notification%20on%20a%20later%20day%3A%20**%7Bnum(_notified%5B_violating%5D.notna().sum())%7D**%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20mo.md(f%22**Violating%20case%20%7B_violating_ids%5B0%5D%7D**%22)%20if%20len(_violating_ids)%20else%20mo.md(%22There%20is%20no%20violating%20case.%22)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20show_case(event_log_s5%2C%20_violating_ids%5B0%5D%2C%20RULE_COLUMNS)%20if%20len(_violating_ids)%20else%20mo.md(%22%22)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Task%206.1c%20-%20Result%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**167%20of%20the%202'894%20applicable%20cases%20violate%20the%20constraint%20(5.77%20%25).**%20118%20of%20them%20have%20no%20notification%20at%20all%2C%20and%2049%20have%20one%20on%20a%20later%20day.%20The%20hypothesis%20of%20very%20few%20violations%20holds%20only%20approximately.%20The%20rule%20has%20a%20precision%20of%200.94%2C%20so%20it%20is%20a%20strong%20pattern%20but%20not%20a%20rule%20of%20the%20process.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Case%20C10130.**%20The%20fine%20of%20131.20%20is%20created%20and%20sent%20on%2007.08.2001%2C%20and%20expenses%20of%206.71%20are%20charged.%20The%20notification%20follows%20only%20on%2015.09.2001%2C%2039%20days%20later.%20The%20fine%20is%20not%20paid%2C%20and%20the%20case%20goes%20on%20to%20a%20penalty%20and%20to%20credit%20collection.%20*Interpretation%3A*%20Unlike%20the%20cases%20in%20Task%205.4d%2C%20this%20is%20apparently%20a%20real%20letter%20by%20post%2C%20because%20there%20are%20postal%20expenses.%20It%20only%20happens%20to%20have%20been%20sent%20on%20the%20day%20the%20fine%20was%20created.%20So%20a%20*Send%20Fine*%20on%20the%20first%20day%20has%20two%20meanings%2C%20and%20the%20log%20can%20only%20separate%20them%20by%20its%20other%20attributes.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Task%206.1d%20-%20Hypothesis%0A%0A%20%20%20%20*If%20the%20outstanding%20amount%20after%20an%20event%20is%200%20or%20less%2C%20then%20there%20is%20no%20further%20event.*%20We%20expect%20**some%20hundreds%20of%20violations**%3A%20Task%204.2b%20showed%20362%20cases%20of%20*Create%20Fine%20%3E%20Payment%20%3E%20Send%20Fine*%2C%20in%20which%20the%20fine%20is%20sent%20after%20it%20was%20paid%2C%20and%20Task%205.1%20showed%20payments%20after%20a%20fine%20was%20settled%2C%20for%20example%20A18543.%20Most%20of%20the%20following%20events%20should%20therefore%20be%20*Send%20Fine*%20or%20*Add%20penalty*.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(%0A%20%20%20%20ACTIVITY%2C%0A%20%20%20%20CASE_ID%2C%0A%20%20%20%20RULE_COLUMNS%2C%0A%20%20%20%20event_log_s5%2C%0A%20%20%20%20mo%2C%0A%20%20%20%20pd%2C%0A%20%20%20%20rule_report%2C%0A%20%20%20%20show_case%2C%0A)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_log%20%3D%20event_log_s5%5B%5BCASE_ID%2C%20ACTIVITY%2C%20'outstanding_amount'%2C%20'local_time'%5D%5D.copy()%0A%20%20%20%20_next%20%3D%20_log.groupby(CASE_ID)%0A%20%20%20%20_log%5B'next_activity'%5D%20%3D%20_next%5BACTIVITY%5D.shift(-1)%0A%20%20%20%20_log%5B'next_time'%5D%20%3D%20_next%5B'local_time'%5D.shift(-1)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20_settled%20%3D%20_log%5B_log%5B'outstanding_amount'%5D%20%3C%3D%200%5D%0A%20%20%20%20_violating_events%20%3D%20_settled%5B_settled%5B'next_activity'%5D.notna()%5D%0A%20%20%20%20_violating_ids%20%3D%20_violating_events%5BCASE_ID%5D.unique()%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20the%20most%20frequent%20kind%20of%20violation%20is%20the%20most%20useful%20one%20to%20inspect%0A%20%20%20%20_pair%20%3D%20_violating_events.groupby(%5BACTIVITY%2C%20'next_activity'%5D).size().idxmax()%0A%20%20%20%20_example%20%3D%20_violating_events%5B(_violating_events%5BACTIVITY%5D%20%3D%3D%20_pair%5B0%5D)%20%26%20(_violating_events%5B'next_activity'%5D%20%3D%3D%20_pair%5B1%5D)%5D%5BCASE_ID%5D.iloc%5B0%5D%0A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.vstack(%5B%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20rule_report(int(_settled%5BCASE_ID%5D.nunique())%2C%20len(_violating_ids))%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20mo.md(f%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20-%20Violating%20events%3A%20**%7Bnum(len(_violating_events))%7D**%0A%20%20%20%20-%20Of%20which%20the%20next%20event%20is%20on%20the%20same%20day%2C%20so%20the%20order%20is%20unknown%20(Task%202.1)%3A%20**%7Bnum((_violating_events%5B'next_time'%5D%20%3D%3D%20_violating_events%5B'local_time'%5D).sum())%7D**%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20mo.md(%22Violating%20events%2C%20by%20the%20activity%20(rows)%20and%20the%20activity%20that%20follows%20it%20(columns)%3A%22)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20pd.crosstab(_violating_events%5BACTIVITY%5D%2C%20_violating_events%5B'next_activity'%5D)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20mo.md(f%22**Violating%20case%20%7B_example%7D**%2C%20of%20the%20most%20frequent%20kind%20(*%7B_pair%5B0%5D%7D*%20followed%20by%20*%7B_pair%5B1%5D%7D*)%22)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20show_case(event_log_s5%2C%20_example%2C%20RULE_COLUMNS)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Task%206.1d%20-%20Result%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**728%20of%20the%2060'783%20applicable%20cases%20violate%20the%20constraint%20(1.20%20%25)**%2C%20with%20774%20violating%20events.%20The%20applicable%20cases%20are%20those%20that%20reach%20an%20outstanding%20amount%20of%200%20or%20less%20at%20some%20event.%20The%20order%20of%20the%20events%20is%20unknown%20for%2033%20of%20them%2C%20because%20they%20are%20on%20the%20same%20day.%20The%20hypothesis%20of%20some%20hundreds%20of%20violations%20is%20confirmed.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Which%20events%20follow%3F**%20Mostly%20*Send%20Fine*%20after%20a%20payment%20(540%20events)%2C%20as%20expected%20from%20Task%204.2b%2C%20then%20a%20further%20*Payment*%20(117)%2C%20which%20leads%20to%20an%20overpayment%2C%20and%20*Add%20penalty*%20after%20a%20payment%20(36).%20We%20expected%20more%20penalties%20here.%20There%20are%20also%2031%20cases%20of%20*Create%20Fine%20%3E%20Send%20Fine*%20in%20which%20the%20amount%20is%20already%200%20or%20less%20when%20the%20fine%20is%20created.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Case%20A1161.**%20The%20fine%20of%2035%20is%20created%20on%2015.08.2006%20and%20paid%20in%20full%20on%2012.12.2006.%20Two%20days%20later%2C%20on%2014.12.2006%2C%20it%20is%20sent%20anyway%2C%20which%20adds%20expenses%20of%2011.%20The%20offender%20pays%20these%20on%2030.12.2006%2C%20and%20then%20nothing%20more%20is%20outstanding.%20*Interpretation%3A*%20The%20letter%20was%20probably%20already%20prepared%20when%20the%20payment%20arrived%2C%20or%20the%20payment%20was%20only%20registered%20later.%20Either%20way%20the%20offender%20pays%20expenses%20for%20a%20letter%20that%20should%20not%20have%20been%20necessary.%20This%20is%20the%20same%20improvement%20as%20in%20Task%204.2c%3A%20check%20for%20payments%20immediately%20before%20sending.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Reflection.**%20With%20a%20precision%20of%200.988%20the%20rule%20is%20nearly%20valid.%20It%20is%20therefore%20useful%20as%20a%20monitoring%20rule%20for%20detecting%20unnecessary%20work.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Task%206.1e%20-%20Hypothesis%0A%0A%20%20%20%20*Credit%20collection%20happens%20not%20earlier%20than%20180%20and%20not%20later%20than%20730%20days%20after%20Insert%20Fine%20Notification.*%20The%20penalty%20comes%20after%2060%20days%2C%20so%20collection%20before%20180%20days%20would%20be%20unusual%2C%20and%20we%20expect%20a%20legal%20limit%20of%20about%20two%20years%20at%20the%20upper%20end.%20We%20expect%20the%20rule%20to%20hold%20for%20**most%20cases%2C%20with%20a%20small%20number%20of%20late%20violations**%2C%20because%20the%20fines%20are%20handed%20over%20in%20batches%20(Task%205.2c).%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(%0A%20%20%20%20RULE_COLUMNS%2C%0A%20%20%20%20day_chart%2C%0A%20%20%20%20delay_days%2C%0A%20%20%20%20event_log_s5%2C%0A%20%20%20%20has_activity%2C%0A%20%20%20%20mo%2C%0A%20%20%20%20rule_report%2C%0A%20%20%20%20show_case%2C%0A)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_days%20%3D%20delay_days('Insert%20Fine%20Notification'%2C%20'Send%20for%20Credit%20Collection')%0A%20%20%20%20_early%2C%20_late%20%3D%20_days%5B_days%20%3C%20180%5D%2C%20_days%5B_days%20%3E%20730%5D%0A%20%20%20%20_without_notification%20%3D%20has_activity('Send%20for%20Credit%20Collection')%20%26%20~has_activity('Insert%20Fine%20Notification')%0A%0A%20%20%20%20_examples%20%3D%20%5B%5D%0A%20%20%20%20if%20len(_early)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_examples%20%2B%3D%20%5Bmo.md(f%22**Earliest%20case%20%7B_early.idxmin()%7D**%20(%7B_early.min()%3Ag%7D%20days)%22)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20show_case(event_log_s5%2C%20_early.idxmin()%2C%20RULE_COLUMNS)%5D%0A%20%20%20%20if%20len(_late)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_examples%20%2B%3D%20%5Bmo.md(f%22**Latest%20case%20%7B_late.idxmax()%7D**%20(%7B_late.max()%3Ag%7D%20days)%22)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20show_case(event_log_s5%2C%20_late.idxmax()%2C%20RULE_COLUMNS)%5D%0A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.vstack(%5B%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20rule_report(len(_days)%2C%20len(_early)%20%2B%20len(_late))%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20mo.md(f%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20-%20Earlier%20than%20180%20days%3A%20**%7Bnum(len(_early))%7D**%2C%20later%20than%20730%20days%3A%20**%7Bnum(len(_late))%7D**%0A%20%20%20%20-%20Median%20**%7B_days.median()%3Ag%7D**%20days%2C%20minimum%20%7B_days.min()%3Ag%7D%2C%20maximum%20%7B_days.max()%3Ag%7D%0A%20%20%20%20-%20Cases%20with%20credit%20collection%20but%20without%20a%20notification%2C%20which%20we%20leave%20out%3A%20**%7Bnum(_without_notification.sum())%7D**%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20day_chart(_days%2C%20'Insert%20Fine%20Notification%20%3E%20Send%20for%20Credit%20Collection')%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20*_examples%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Task%206.1e%20-%20Result%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**11'258%20of%20the%2059'013%20applicable%20cases%20violate%20the%20constraint%20(19.08%20%25).**%20All%20of%20them%20are%20too%20late%2C%20none%20is%20too%20early.%20Every%20case%20with%20credit%20collection%20also%20has%20a%20notification.%20Our%20hypothesis%20of%20a%20small%20number%20of%20violations%20is%20refuted.%20The%20rule%20is%20clearly%20not%20kept%20in%20practice%2C%20even%20though%20the%20median%20of%20548%20days%20lies%20well%20inside%20the%20limits.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20-%20**Lower%20limit%20(180%20days)%3A**%20It%20is%20always%20kept.%20The%20shortest%20delay%20is%20269%20days.%20So%20the%20limit%20could%20be%20reached%20far%20earlier%20in%20principle%2C%20but%20this%20is%20never%20used.%0A%20%20%20%20-%20**Upper%20limit%20(730%20days)%3A**%20About%20one%20in%20five%20cases%20is%20late%2C%20with%20a%20maximum%20of%203'391%20days.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Case%20N40905%20(the%20latest%20one).**%20A%20fine%20of%2019%20is%20created%20on%2028.10.2002%2C%20notified%20on%2013.12.2002%20and%20raised%20by%20the%20penalty%20on%2011.02.2003.%20It%20is%20then%20handed%20over%20only%20on%2026.03.2012%2C%20more%20than%20**nine%20years**%20after%20the%20notification%20and%20for%20only%2049.%20*Interpretation%3A*%20The%20case%20was%20skipped%20by%20many%20batches%20(Task%205.5).%20If%20the%20constraint%20is%20a%20legal%20limit%2C%20such%20a%20claim%20could%20no%20longer%20be%20enforceable%2C%20and%20the%20cost%20of%20collecting%20it%20could%20easily%20exceed%20its%20value.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Reflection.**%20The%20late%20cases%20are%20a%20direct%20result%20of%20the%20rare%20and%20non-FIFO%20batches.%20More%20regular%20hand-overs%20(Task%205.4b)%2C%20combined%20with%20a%20check%20of%20the%20oldest%20cases%20first%2C%20would%20remove%20most%20of%20these%20violations.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Task%206.2%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Task%206.2%20-%20Constraint%20and%20hypothesis%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Constraint%3A**%20*Add%20penalty%20happens%20exactly%2060%20days%20after%20Insert%20Fine%20Notification.*%0A%0A%20%20%20%20We%20expect%20this%20to%20be%20satisfied%20in%20almost%20all%20cases.%20It%20would%20show%20that%20the%20penalty%20is%20added%20automatically%20on%20a%20fixed%20date%2C%20which%20matters%20for%20the%20penalties%20on%20nearly%20paid%20fines%20in%20Task%205.1.%20We%20expect%20exceptions%20at%20most%20where%20appeals%20interrupt%20the%20process.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(%0A%20%20%20%20RULE_COLUMNS%2C%0A%20%20%20%20case_log_s5%2C%0A%20%20%20%20delay_days%2C%0A%20%20%20%20event_log_s5%2C%0A%20%20%20%20mo%2C%0A%20%20%20%20rule_report%2C%0A%20%20%20%20show_case%2C%0A)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_days%20%3D%20delay_days('Insert%20Fine%20Notification'%2C%20'Add%20penalty')%0A%20%20%20%20_other%20%3D%20_days%5B_days%20!%3D%2060%5D%0A%0A%20%20%20%20_top%20%3D%20_days.value_counts().head(10).rename('cases').rename_axis('days').to_frame()%0A%20%20%20%20_top%5B'share%20%25'%5D%20%3D%20(100%20*%20_top%5B'cases'%5D%20%2F%20len(_days)).round(2)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20are%20the%20exceptions%20cases%20with%20an%20appeal%3F%0A%20%20%20%20_appeal_activities%20%3D%20%5B'Appeal%20to%20Judge'%2C%20'Insert%20Date%20Appeal%20to%20Prefecture'%5D%0A%20%20%20%20_exception_has_appeal%20%3D%20case_log_s5.loc%5B_other.index%2C%20'seq_variant'%5D.apply(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20lambda%20variant%3A%20any(_a%20in%20variant%20for%20_a%20in%20_appeal_activities))%0A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.vstack(%5B%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20rule_report(len(_days)%2C%20len(_other))%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20mo.md(f%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20-%20Exceptions%20that%20contain%20an%20appeal%3A%20**%7Bnum(_exception_has_appeal.sum())%7D**%20of%20%7Bnum(len(_other))%7D%0A%20%20%20%20-%20Delay%20between%20the%20two%20activities%2C%20shortest%20and%20longest%3A%20**%7B_days.min()%3Ag%7D**%20and%20**%7B_days.max()%3Ag%7D**%20days%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20mo.md(%22The%2010%20most%20frequent%20delays%3A%22)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_top%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20mo.md(f%22**Exception%20%7B_other.index%5B0%5D%7D**%22)%20if%20len(_other)%20else%20mo.md(%22There%20is%20no%20exception.%22)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20show_case(event_log_s5%2C%20_other.index%5B0%5D%2C%20RULE_COLUMNS)%20if%20len(_other)%20else%20mo.md(%22%22)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Task%206.2%20-%20Result%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**0%20of%20the%2079'860%20applicable%20cases%20violate%20the%20constraint.**%20All%20of%20them%20have%20exactly%2060%20days%20between%20the%20two%20activities%2C%20even%20more%20than%20we%20expected.%20There%20are%20no%20exceptions%20for%20appeals%20either.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Reflection.**%20In%20real%20work%2C%20a%20delay%20of%20exactly%20the%20same%20length%20in%20every%20case%2C%20including%20weekends%20and%20holidays%2C%20is%20not%20plausible.%20At%20least%20one%20of%20the%20two%20dates%20must%20therefore%20be%20calculated%20by%20the%20system%2C%20not%20observed%3A%20the%20penalty%20is%20set%20for%20day%2060%2C%20or%20one%20of%20the%20two%20events%20is%20entered%20afterwards.%20Together%20with%20Task%206.1a%20this%20has%20three%20consequences%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20-%20It%20supports%20our%20hypothesis%20in%20Task%205.1%20that%20the%20penalty%20is%20added%20automatically%20on%20a%20fixed%20date%2C%20so%20that%20it%20also%20hits%20offenders%20who%20have%20paid%20almost%20everything%20or%20who%20pay%20right%20around%20this%20time.%0A%20%20%20%20-%20This%20delay%20should%20not%20be%20counted%20as%20waiting%20time%20that%20can%20be%20improved%2C%20because%20it%20results%20from%20the%20rule%20itself.%0A%20%20%20%20-%20*Insert%20Fine%20Notification*%20may%20not%20reliably%20show%20the%20actual%20delivery%20date.%20The%20transit%20times%20in%20Task%205.4d%20should%20therefore%20be%20read%20with%20care.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20*Recommendation%20data%20collection%3A*%20Record%20the%20real%20time%20of%20the%20delivery%20and%20the%20rule%20that%20triggered%20the%20penalty.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Task%206.3%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Task%206.3%20-%20Approach%20and%20hypothesis%0A%0A%20%20%20%20We%20convert%20our%20BPMN%20model%20from%20Task%204.3%20into%20a%20Petri%20net%20and%20align%20each%20of%20the%2048%20variants%20of%20the%20fine%20object%20sub-log%20with%20it.%20An%20alignment%20shows%20which%20steps%20of%20a%20variant%20the%20model%20cannot%20follow.%20Black%20transitions%20of%20the%20Petri%20net%20appear%20as%20%60None%60%20and%20are%20ignored.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20From%20Task%204.3%20we%20expect%20about%2031%20of%20the%2048%20variants%20not%20to%20fit.%20We%20expect%20some%20of%20them%20to%20be%20behaviour%20that%20the%20model%20should%20allow.%20Our%20candidate%20is%20a%20fine%20that%20is%20partly%20paid%20and%20then%20sent%20to%20credit%20collection%3A%20*Create%20Fine%20%3E%20Send%20Fine%20%3E%20Insert%20Fine%20Notifica 5%20cases%20contain%20a%20*Payment*%2C%20and%20one%20ends%20with%20an%20appeal%20to%20the%20prefecture.%20Only%20the%208%20cases%20of%20the%20variant%20*Create%20Fine%20%3E%20Send%20Fine*%20could%20be%20fines%20that%20were%20dropped%20because%20the%20letter%20was%20late%2C%20and%20the%20log%20does%20not%20show%20whether%20this%20was%20the%20reason.%20All%2021%20false%20positives%20follow%20the%20standard%20sequence%20up%20to%20*Send%20for%20Credit%20Collection*.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Case%20A16236%20(false%20positive).**%20A%20fine%20of%2036%20is%20created%20on%2003.08.2007%20and%20sent%20only%20on%2018.11.2008%2C%20473%20days%20later.%20It%20is%20notified%20on%2020.12.2008%2C%20the%20penalty%20follows%2060%20days%20later%20on%2018.02.2009%2C%20and%20on%2015.10.2010%20the%20outstanding%2087.50%20are%20sent%20for%20credit%20collection.%20Nothing%20in%20the%20log%20shows%20that%20the%20late%20letter%20was%20noticed.%20*Interpretation%3A*%20Like%20the%20penalty%2C%20the%20hand-over%20to%20credit%20collection%20seems%20to%20be%20decided%20without%20checking%20when%20the%20letter%20was%20sent.%20Under%20the%20real%20deadline%20of%20150%20days%20(Task%205.4c)%20such%20a%20fine%20should%20not%20be%20valid%20(our%20assumption%2C%20not%20checked%20against%20the%20legal%20text)%2C%20so%20the%20offender%20could%20contest%20the%20collection.%20*Improvement%20of%20the%20process%3A*%20check%20the%20date%20of%20the%20letter%20before%20a%20fine%20is%20sent%20for%20credit%20collection.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Task%207.2%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Task%207.2%20-%20Hypothesis%0A%0A%20%20%20%20*If%20a%20case%20has%20a%20dismissal%20value%20other%20than%20NIL%2C%20%60%23%60%20and%20%60G%60%2C%20then%20it%20is%20of%20the%20variant%20Create%20Fine%20%3E%20Send%20Fine.*%20The%20description%20of%20the%20log%20only%20documents%20%60%23%60%20(prefecture)%20and%20%60G%60%20(judge)%2C%20but%20Task%202.5%20(Part%202)%20and%20Task%203.1%20showed%20that%20other%20codes%20occur%3A%202'577%20cases%20have%20a%20value%20other%20than%20NIL%2C%20and%202'073%20of%20them%20are%20dismissed%20with%20%60%23%60%20or%20%60G%60%2C%20which%20leaves%20about%20500%20cases%20with%20other%20codes.%20A%20fine%20that%20the%20police%20itself%20cancels%20before%20it%20is%20notified%20would%20stop%20after%20*Send%20Fine*%20and%20needs%20a%20code%20of%20its%20own%2C%20so%20we%20expect%20most%20of%20these%20codes%20to%20occur%20only%20in%20this%20variant.%20A%20code%20that%20also%20occurs%20in%20cases%20with%20a%20notification%2C%20an%20appeal%20or%20a%20payment%20cannot%20mean%20such%20a%20dismissal%20by%20the%20police%20and%20is%20excluded.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20As%20the%20dismissal%20value%20of%20a%20case%20we%20use%20its%20latest%20value.%20This%20is%20the%20value%20of%20*Create%20Fine*%2C%20unless%20an%20appeal%20changes%20it%20later%20(only%20to%20%60%23%60%20or%20%60G%60).%20We%20expect%20a%20small%20recall%2C%20because%20the%20variant%20has%2020'385%20cases%20and%20only%20about%20500%20cases%20have%20one%20of%20the%20other%20codes.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(CASE_ID%2C%20case_log_s5%2C%20event_log_s5%2C%20mo%2C%20pd)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20outcome%3A%20the%20case%20is%20of%20the%20variant%20Create%20Fine%20%3E%20Send%20Fine%0A%20%20%20%20only_sent%20%3D%20case_log_s5%5B'seq_variant'%5D%20%3D%3D%20('Create%20Fine'%2C%20'Send%20Fine')%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20dismissal%20value%20of%20a%20case%3A%20its%20latest%20value%2C%20i.e.%20the%20value%20of%20Create%20Fine%20unless%20an%20appeal%20changed%20it%0A%20%20%20%20case_dismissal%20%3D%20(event_log_s5.dropna(subset%3D%5B'dismissal'%5D).groupby(CASE_ID)%5B'dismissal'%5D.last()%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20.reindex(case_log_s5.index))%0A%0A%20%20%20%20_table%20%3D%20pd.crosstab(case_dismissal%2C%20only_sent).rename(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20columns%3D%7BTrue%3A%20'cases%20of%20the%20variant'%2C%20False%3A%20'other%20cases'%7D).rename_axis(index%3D'dismissal'%2C%20columns%3DNone)%0A%20%20%20%20_table%5B'precision'%5D%20%3D%20(_table%5B'cases%20of%20the%20variant'%5D%20%2F%20(_table%5B'cases%20of%20the%20variant'%5D%20%2B%20_table%5B'other%20cases'%5D)).round(4)%0A%20%20%20%20_table%20%3D%20_table.sort_values(%5B'precision'%2C%20'cases%20of%20the%20variant'%5D%2C%20ascending%3DFalse)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20maximal%20set%20with%20precision%201.0%3A%20every%20value%20whose%20cases%20all%20belong%20to%20the%20variant%0A%20%20%20%20POLICE_DISMISSAL%20%3D%20sorted(_table.index%5B_table%5B'other%20cases'%5D%20%3D%3D%200%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20_explanation%20%3D%20case_dismissal.isin(POLICE_DISMISSAL)%0A%20%20%20%20_tp%20%3D%20_explanation%20%26%20only_sent%0A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.vstack(%5B%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20mo.md(%22Cases%20per%20dismissal%20value%20(latest%20value%20of%20the%20case)%20and%20variant%3A%22)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_table%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20mo.md(f%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20-%20Maximal%20set%20with%20precision%201.0%3A%20**%7B'%2C%20'.join(POLICE_DISMISSAL)%7D**%20(%7Blen(POLICE_DISMISSAL)%7D%20values)%0A%20%20%20%20-%20Cases%20with%20one%20of%20these%20values%3A%20**%7Bnum(_explanation.sum())%7D**%2C%20of%20which%20of%20the%20variant%3A%20**%7Bnum(_tp.sum())%7D**%0A%20%20%20%20-%20**Precision%3A%20%7B_tp.sum()%20%2F%20_explanation.sum()%3A.4f%7D**%0A%20%20%20%20-%20**Recalled%20cases%3A%20%7Bnum(_tp.sum())%7D**%20of%20%7Bnum(only_sent.sum())%7D%20cases%20of%20the%20variant%20(recall%20%7B_tp.sum()%20%2F%20only_sent.sum()%3A.2%25%7D)%0A%20%20%20%20-%20Cases%20of%20the%20variant%20without%20one%20of%20these%20values%3A%20**%7Bnum((only_sent%20%26%20~_explanation).sum())%7D**%2C%20of%20which%20with%20dismissal%20value%20NIL%3A%20**%7Bnum((only_sent%20%26%20(case_dismissal%20%3D%3D%20'NIL')).sum())%7D**%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20return%20case_dismissal%2C%20only_sent%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Task%207.2%20-%20Result%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**The%20maximal%20set%20is%20%7B2%2C%203%2C%205%2C%20A%2C%20B%2C%20E%2C%20F%2C%20I%2C%20J%2C%20K%2C%20M%2C%20N%2C%20Q%2C%20R%2C%20T%2C%20U%2C%20V%7D%20(17%20values).%20It%20explains%20the%20variant%20with%20precision%201.0%20and%20recalls%20444%20of%20its%2020'385%20cases%20(2.18%20%25).**%20The%20hypothesis%20is%20confirmed%3A%20most%20of%20the%20undocumented%20codes%20occur%20only%20in%20this%20variant.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20set%20is%20maximal%2C%20because%20every%20other%20value%20of%20the%20log%20also%20occurs%20outside%20the%20variant%3A%20%60D%60%20(31%20cases%20in%20the%20variant%2C%203%20outside)%2C%20%60C%60%20(6%20and%202)%2C%20%60Z%60%20(5%20and%201)%2C%20%60%40%60%2C%20%60%24%60%20and%20%604%60%20(only%20outside)%2C%20as%20well%20as%20NIL%2C%20%60%23%60%20and%20%60G%60.%20Adding%20any%20of%20them%20would%20add%20a%20false%20positive.%20Since%20a%20value%20can%20only%20belong%20to%20the%20set%20if%20all%20of%20its%20cases%20are%20of%20the%20variant%2C%20there%20is%20exactly%20one%20maximal%20set.%20The%20most%20frequent%20values%20in%20it%20are%20%60A%60%20(213%20cases)%2C%20%60T%60%20(111)%2C%20%60I%60%20(29)%20and%20%60N%60%20(28).%20The%20cases%20outside%20the%20variant%20with%20%60D%60%2C%20%60C%60%20and%20%60Z%60%20contain%20an%20appeal%20to%20the%20prefecture%2C%20a%20payment%20or%20a%20credit%20collection.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20explanation%20leaves%2019'941%20cases%20of%20the%20variant%20unexplained%2C%20and%2019'899%20of%20them%20have%20the%20value%20NIL%2C%20i.e.%20no%20code%20at%20all.%20*Interpretation%3A*%20The%20codes%20seem%20to%20record%20why%20the%20police%20dropped%20a%20fine%2C%20but%20the%20log%20does%20not%20document%20their%20meaning%2C%20and%20for%20most%20fines%20of%20this%20variant%20no%20code%20was%20entered.%20This%20supports%20the%20assumption%20of%20Task%207.3%20that%20the%20code%20was%20forgotten%20in%20these%20cases.%20*Recommendation%20data%20collection%3A*%20Document%20the%20dismissal%20codes%2C%20and%20require%20a%20code%20when%20a%20fine%20is%20closed%20without%20payment%20or%20credit%20collection.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Task%207.3%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Task%207.3%20-%20Approach%20and%20hypothesis%0A%0A%20%20%20%20We%20follow%20the%20assumption%20of%20the%20task%3A%20all%20cases%20of%20the%20variant%20*Create%20Fine%20%3E%20Send%20Fine*%20are%20dismissed%20by%20the%20police%20(Task%207.2).%20The%20search%20for%20explanations%20is%20done%20in%20the%20rule%20induction%20notebook%20%60rule_induction_road_fines_marimo_iox.py%60%20(html%20export%20in%20the%20submission)%2C%20in%20four%20steps%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20**Baseline.**%20We%20keep%20only%20the%20unresolved%20cases%3A%20not%20of%20the%20variant%20*Create%20Fine%20%3E%20Send%20Fine*%2C%20not%20dismissed%20by%20a%20judge%20or%20the%20prefecture%20(%60dismissal%60%20%60G%60%20or%20%60%23%60)%2C%20and%20not%20fully%20paid%20(fine%20amount%20plus%20expenses%20minus%20payments%20is%20above%200).%20The%20outcome%20to%20explain%20is%20%22not%20sent%20for%20credit%20collection%22.%0A%20%20%20%202.%20**Hiding.**%20We%20hide%20%60collected%60%2C%20%60Send_for_Credit_Collection%3A%3Acount%60%20and%20the%20variant%2C%20because%20they%20contain%20the%20outcome.%20The%20first%20induction%20then%20proposed%20rules%20with%20%60duration%60%2C%20%60end_time%60%20and%20%60no_of_events%60%2C%20for%20example%20%22%60duration%60%20at%20most%20383%20days%22.%20These%20features%20are%20measured%20over%20the%20whole%20case%2C%20including%20a%20later%20*Send%20for%20Credit%20Collection*.%20Since%20the%20hand-over%20comes%20about%2016%20months%20after%20the%20penalty%20(Task%205.4a)%2C%20a%20short%20case%20is%20almost%20by%20definition%20not%20collected.%20We%20hide%20them%20as%20well.%0A%20%20%20%203.%20**Rule%20induction.**%20Among%20the%20rules%20suggested%20on%20the%20remaining%20features%20we%20store%20those%20that%20are%20meaningful%20from%20a%20business%20point%20of%20view.%20After%20each%20stored%20rule%20the%20suggestions%20are%20induced%20again%20on%20the%20cases%20that%20are%20still%20unclaimed.%20Where%20a%20suggested%20rule%20contains%20a%20condition%20without%20a%20business%20reason%2C%20we%20drop%20that%20condition%20and%20keep%20the%20rule%20only%20if%20its%20precision%20stays%20above%200.95.%0A%20%20%20%204.%20**Case%20inspection.**%20We%20check%20the%20stored%20rules%20below%20on%20their%20recalled%20cases.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Hypothesis.**%20From%20the%20earlier%20tasks%20we%20expect%20two%20kinds%20of%20unresolved%20cases%20that%20are%20not%20collected%3A%20appeals%20to%20the%20prefecture%20without%20a%20recorded%20result%20(Task%206.1b%20found%203'224%20appeals%20that%20are%20never%20followed%20by%20a%20result)%2C%20and%20fines%20with%20a%20small%20rest%20after%20a%20payment%20(Task%202.5%20of%20Part%202%20showed%20many%20payments%20that%20leave%20an%20amount%20outstanding).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Below%20we%20evaluate%20the%20stored%20rules%20again%20with%20our%20own%20code%20on%20the%20same%20population%2C%20independently%20of%20the%20rule%20induction%20notebook.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(%0A%20%20%20%20CASE_ID%2C%0A%20%20%20%20case_dismissal%2C%0A%20%20%20%20case_log_s5%2C%0A%20%20%20%20event_log_s5%2C%0A%20%20%20%20has_activity%2C%0A%20%20%20%20mo%2C%0A%20%20%20%20only_sent%2C%0A%20%20%20%20pd%2C%0A)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20the%20same%20population%20as%20in%20the%20rule%20induction%20notebook%20(cell%202.2%20there)%3A%20not%20of%20the%20variant%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20Create%20Fine%20%3E%20Send%20Fine%2C%20not%20dismissed%20by%20a%20judge%20or%20the%20prefecture%2C%20and%20not%20fully%20paid%0A%20%20%20%20_cases%20%3D%20event_log_s5.groupby(CASE_ID)%0A%20%20%20%20_owed%20%3D%20(_cases%5B'amount'%5D.last()%20%2B%20_cases%5B'expense'%5D.sum()%20-%20_cases%5B'paymentAmount'%5D.sum()).reindex(case_log_s5.index)%0A%20%20%20%20_fully_paid%20%3D%20_owed.round(2)%20%3C%3D%200%0A%20%20%20%20_dismissed%20%3D%20case_dismissal.isin(%5B'%23'%2C%20'G'%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20unresolved%20%3D%20~only_sent%20%26%20~_dismissed%20%26%20~_fully_paid%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20outcome%3A%20an%20unresolved%20case%20is%20not%20sent%20for%20credit%20collection%0A%20%20%20%20not_collected_73%20%3D%20unresolved%20%26%20~case_log_s5%5B'credit_collection'%5D%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20the%20three%20rules%20we%20stored%20in%20the%20rule%20induction%20notebook%0A%20%20%20%20rule_open_appeal%20%3D%20(has_activity('Insert%20Date%20Appeal%20to%20Prefecture')%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%26%20~has_activity('Notify%20Result%20Appeal%20to%20Offender'))%0A%20%20%20%20rule_not_notified%20%3D%20~has_activity('Insert%20Fine%20Notification')%0A%20%20%20%20n_payments_73%20%3D%20case_log_s5%5B'seq_variant'%5D.apply(lambda%20variant%3A%20variant.count('Payment'))%0A%20%20%20%20rule_two_payments%20%3D%20n_payments_73%20%3E%3D%202%0A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20def%20_evaluate(name%2C%20rule)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_claimed%20%3D%20rule%20%26%20unresolved%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_tp%20%3D%20int((_claimed%20%26%20not_collected_73).sum())%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20return%20%7B'rule'%3A%20name%2C%20'claimed%20cases'%3A%20int(_claimed.sum())%2C%20'true%20positives%20(recalled)'%3A%20_tp%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20'false%20positives'%3A%20int(_claimed.sum())%20-%20_tp%2C%20'precision'%3A%20round(_tp%20%2F%20_claimed.sum()%2C%204)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20'recall%20%25'%3A%20round(100%20*%20_tp%20%2F%20not_collected_73.sum()%2C%202)%7D%0A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20_rules%20%3D%20pd.DataFrame(%5B%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_evaluate('1%3A%20open%20appeal%20to%20the%20prefecture'%2C%20rule_open_appeal)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_evaluate('2%3A%20fine%20never%20notified'%2C%20rule_not_notified)%2C%0A%20 %20_table%20%3D%20pd.DataFrame(%7B'cases'%3A%20_counts%7D)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_table.index%20%3D%20%5B'%20%3E%20'.join(_variant)%20for%20_variant%20in%20_table.index%5D%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20return%20_table%0A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20_appeal_ids%20%3D%20case_log_s5.index%5Brule_open_appeal%20%26%20not_collected_73%5D%0A%20%20%20%20_two_payments%20%3D%20rule_two_payments%20%26%20not_collected_73%0A%20%20%20%20_rest%20%3D%20case_log_s5.loc%5B_two_payments%2C%20'final_outstanding_amount'%5D%0A%20%20%20%20_appeal_year%20%3D%20case_log_s5.loc%5B_appeal_ids%2C%20'start'%5D.dt.year.value_counts().sort_index().rename('cases')%0A%20%20%20%20_appeal_year.index%20%3D%20_appeal_year.index.astype(str)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.vstack(%5B%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20mo.md(%22**Rule%201%20(open%20appeal)%3A**%20most%20frequent%20sequences%20of%20the%20recalled%20cases%22)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_variants(rule_open_appeal)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20mo.md(%22Recalled%20cases%20of%20rule%201%20by%20year%20of%20*Create%20Fine*%3A%22)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_appeal_year.to_frame().T%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20mo.md(f%22**Case%20%7B_appeal_ids%5B0%5D%7D%20(rule%201)**%22)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20show_case(event_log_s5%2C%20_appeal_ids%5B0%5D%2C%20RULE_COLUMNS)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20mo.md(%22**Rule%202%20(never%20notified)%3A**%20most%20frequent%20sequences%20of%20the%20recalled%20cases%22)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_variants(rule_not_notified)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20mo.md(%22**Case%20A127%20(rule%202)%2C%20the%20case%20of%20Task%204.2c**%22)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20show_case(event_log_s5%2C%20'A127'%2C%20RULE_COLUMNS)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20mo.md(%22**Rule%203%20(at%20least%20two%20payments)%3A**%20most%20frequent%20sequences%20of%20the%20recalled%20cases%22)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_variants(rule_two_payments)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20mo.md(f%22Outstanding%20amount%20at%20the%20end%20of%20the%20recalled%20cases%20of%20rule%203%3A%20median%20**%7B_rest.median()%3Ag%7D**%2C%20quartiles%20%7B_rest.quantile(0.25)%3Ag%7D%20and%20%7B_rest.quantile(0.75)%3Ag%7D%22)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20mo.md(%22**Case%20A10798%20(rule%203)%2C%20the%20case%20of%20Task%205.1b**%22)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20show_case(event_log_s5%2C%20'A10798'%2C%20RULE_COLUMNS)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Task%207.3%20-%20Result%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20population%20has%20**67'635%20unresolved%20cases%2C%20of%20which%208'625%20are%20not%20sent%20for%20credit%20collection**%20(the%20same%20numbers%20as%20in%20the%20rule%20induction%20notebook).%20We%20found%20**three%20explanations%20of%20type%20(a)**%2C%20each%20with%20a%20precision%20above%200.99%20and%20well%20above%20200%20recalled%20cases%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%7C%20Explanation%20%7C%20Precision%20%7C%20Recalled%20cases%20%7C%20False%20positives%20%7C%0A%20%20%20%20%7C---%7C---%7C---%7C---%7C%0A%20%20%20%20%7C%201%3A%20open%20appeal%20to%20the%20prefecture%20%7C%201.0000%20%7C%201'284%20%7C%200%20%7C%0A%20%20%20%20%7C%202%3A%20fine%20never%20notified%20%7C%201.0000%20%7C%20704%20%7C%200%20%7C%0A%20%20%20%20%7C%203%3A%20at%20least%20two%20payments%20%7C%200.9941%20%7C%203'697%20%7C%2022%20%7C%0A%20%20%20%20%7C%201%2C%202%20or%203%20%7C%200.9961%20%7C%205'608%20(65.02%20%25%20of%20the%20outcome)%20%7C%2022%20%7C%0A%0A%20%20%20%2064%20cases%20match%20rules%201%20and%202%2C%2013%20match%20rules%201%20and%203%2C%20and%20none%20matches%20rules%202%20and%203.%20In%20the%20rule%20induction%20notebook%2C%20where%20the%20rules%20are%20stored%20one%20after%20the%20other%2C%20the%20second%20rule%20therefore%20recalls%20640%20additional%20cases%20after%20the%20first%20one%2C%20and%20the%20third%20rule%203'684%20more.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Explanation%201%3A%20*If%20an%20appeal%20to%20the%20prefecture%20has%20been%20filed%20and%20its%20result%20has%20not%20been%20notified%20to%20the%20offender%2C%20then%20the%20case%20is%20not%20sent%20for%20credit%20collection.***%20(*Insert%20Date%20Appeal%20to%20Prefecture*%20at%20least%20once%20and%20no%20*Notify%20Result%20Appeal%20to%20Offender*.)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20-%20*Why%20meaningful%3A*%20While%20an%20appeal%20is%20undecided%2C%20the%20fine%20is%20contested%2C%20and%20it%20would%20be%20unfair%20to%20hand%20it%20over%20to%20a%20collection%20agency.%20The%20rule%20describes%20a%20waiting%20state%20of%20the%20process.%0A%20%20%20%20-%20*How%20we%20obtained%20it%3A*%20baseline%2C%20hiding%20of%20the%20outcome%20features%20and%20of%20the%20three%20time%20and%20size%20features%2C%20then%20rule%20induction%20(the%20rule%20was%20suggested%20as%20is).%20Case%20inspection%20below.%0A%20%20%20%20-%20*Case%20inspection%3A*%201'170%20of%20the%201'284%20cases%20end%20with%20*Send%20Appeal%20to%20Prefecture*%2C%20and%20the%20cases%20come%20from%20all%20years%20(193%20from%202000%2C%20135%20from%202012).%20So%20most%20of%20these%20appeals%20are%20not%20running%20at%20the%20end%20of%20the%20log%2C%20they%20simply%20never%20get%20a%20result%20in%20the%20log%2C%20as%20already%20seen%20in%20Task%206.1b.%20In%20case%20A10125%20a%20fine%20of%2036%20is%20sent%20with%20expenses%20of%2013%20and%20notified%20on%2026.07.2007.%20The%20offender%20appeals%20on%2001.08.2007%20and%20pays%20the%20full%2049%20on%2014.09.2007.%20On%2024.09.2007%2C%2060%20days%20after%20the%20notification%2C%20the%20penalty%20is%20added%20anyway%2C%20which%20leaves%2038%20outstanding%2C%20and%20on%20the%20same%20day%20the%20appeal%20is%20sent%20to%20the%20prefecture.%20Nothing%20follows.%20*Interpretation%3A*%20The%20appeal%20stops%20the%20collection%2C%20but%20because%20the%20result%20is%20never%20recorded%2C%20the%2038%20stay%20open%20forever.%20Whether%20the%20prefecture%20decided%20at%20all%2C%20the%20log%20does%20not%20show.%20*Recommendation%20data%20collection%3A*%20record%20the%20result%20of%20every%20appeal%20(see%20Task%206.1b).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Explanation%202%3A%20*If%20a%20fine%20has%20never%20been%20notified%2C%20then%20the%20case%20is%20not%20sent%20for%20credit%20collection.***%20(no%20*Insert%20Fine%20Notification*.)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20-%20*Why%20meaningful%3A*%20The%20penalty%20is%20added%2060%20days%20after%20the%20notification%20(Task%205.4a)%2C%20and%20credit%20collection%20follows%20the%20penalty.%20Without%20a%20notification%20the%20fine%20never%20reaches%20this%20part%20of%20the%20process%2C%20and%20an%20offender%20who%20was%20never%20notified%20cannot%20be%20pursued.%0A%20%20%20%20-%20*How%20we%20obtained%20it%3A*%20the%20same%20steps.%20The%20rule%20was%20suggested%20as%20is%2C%20before%20and%20after%20the%20first%20rule%20had%20been%20stored.%0A%20%20%20%20-%20*Case%20inspection%3A*%20The%20most%20frequent%20sequences%20are%20*Create%20Fine%20%3E%20Payment%20%3E%20Send%20Fine*%20(343%20cases)%2C%20*Create%20Fine%20%3E%20Send%20Fine%20%3E%20Payment*%20(236)%20and%20*Create%20Fine%20%3E%20Payment*%20(56)%2C%20so%20the%20offender%20paid%20before%20or%20right%20after%20the%20letter.%20What%20remains%20is%20small%3A%20the%20median%20outstanding%20amount%20is%206.71%20and%20three%20quarters%20of%20the%20cases%20have%2010%20or%20less.%206.71%20is%20exactly%20the%20expense%20of%20a%20letter%20in%202001%20(Task%202.7)%2C%20and%20568%20of%20the%20704%20cases%20are%20from%202000%20to%202002.%20In%20372%20of%20the%20704%20cases%20exactly%20the%20expense%20of%20the%20letter%20remains.%20Case%20A127%20(Task%204.2c)%20is%20typical%3A%20the%20offender%20pays%20the%20full%20fine%20of%2035%20on%2004.08.2006%2C%20two%20days%20after%20it%20was%20created.%20The%20letter%20follows%20on%2012.12.2006%20anyway%20and%20adds%20expenses%20of%2011%2C%20which%20are%20never%20paid.%20*Interpretation%3A*%20These%20fines%20were%20paid%20early%2C%20and%20what%20remains%20is%20mostly%20the%20postage%20of%20a%20letter%20sent%20afterwards.%20The%20police%20does%20not%20notify%20them%2C%20so%20they%20never%20get%20a%20penalty%20and%20are%20never%20collected.%20From%20a%20business%20point%20of%20view%20they%20are%20settled%2C%20although%20the%20log%20shows%20a%20small%20amount%20outstanding.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Explanation%203%3A%20*If%20the%20offender%20has%20made%20at%20least%20two%20payments%2C%20then%20the%20case%20is%20not%20sent%20for%20credit%20collection.***%20(*Payment*%20at%20least%20twice.)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20-%20*Why%20meaningful%3A*%20The%20recalled%20cases%20are%20the%20pattern%20of%20Task%205.1b%3A%20the%20offender%20pays%20the%20fine%20and%20its%20expenses%20in%20two%20steps%2C%20mostly%20one%20payment%20before%20and%20one%20after%20the%20penalty%20(3'239%20cases%20of%20the%20sequence%20*...%20Insert%20Fine%20Notification%20%3E%20Payment%20%3E%20Add%20penalty%20%3E%20Payment*).%20In%203'687%20of%20the%203'697%20cases%20the%20payments%20add%20up%20to%20at%20least%20the%20initial%20fine%20plus%20expenses%20(%C2%B1%201)%2C%20and%20the%20rest%20is%20close%20to%20the%20penalty%20(median%2035.17%2C%20quartiles%2031.30%20and%2036.50).%20So%20the%20offender%20paid%20what%20the%20original%20notice%20asked%20for%2C%20and%20only%20the%20penalty%20stays%20open.%0A%20%20%20%20-%20*How%20we%20obtained%20it%3A*%20the%20same%20baseline%20and%20hiding%2C%20then%20rule%20induction%20after%20the%20first%20two%20rules%20had%20been%20stored.%20The%20suggested%20rule%20was%20%22at%20least%20two%20payments%20and%20*Create%20Fine*%20before%20about%20September%202003%22%20(precision%200.999%2C%202'081%20cases).%20We%20found%20no%20business%20reason%20for%20the%20date%20limit%20and%20dropped%20it%3B%20without%20it%20the%20rule%20keeps%20a%20precision%20of%200.9941%20and%20recalls%203'697%20cases.%20Case%20inspection%20below.%0A%20%20%20%20-%20*Case%20inspection%3A*%20In%20case%20A10798%20(Task%205.1b)%20the%20offender%20pays%2022%20of%20the%2035%20on%2025.09.2007%2C%20the%20penalty%20is%20added%20on%2010.10.2007%2C%20and%20ten%20days%20later%20the%20offender%20pays%20the%20missing%2013.%20The%20case%20ends%20with%2022%20outstanding%2C%20exactly%20the%20penalty%2C%20and%20is%20never%20handed%20over.%20The%2022%20false%20positives%20are%20cases%20with%20two%20or%20more%20payments%20that%20are%20sent%20for%20credit%20collection%20anyway.%20*Interpretation%3A*%20Apparently%20the%20police%20does%20not%20hand%20over%20a%20penalty%20that%20remains%20after%20the%20original%20amount%20was%20paid%20in%20two%20steps.%20Why%20a%20single%20payment%20is%20handed%20over%20much%20more%20often%20(precision%20of%20%22exactly%20one%20payment%22%3A%200.632)%2C%20the%20log%20does%20not%20show.%20*Question%3A*%20Is%20the%20remaining%20penalty%20waived%2C%20for%20example%20because%20the%20first%20payment%20was%20made%20in%20time%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Hypothesis.**%20Confirmed.%20The%20appeals%20without%20a%20result%20are%20explanation%201.%20The%20small%20rest%20after%20a%20payment%20appears%20twice%3A%20as%20postage%20for%20fines%20without%20notification%20(explanation%202)%20and%20as%20a%20remaining%20penalty%20after%20two%20payments%20(explanation%203).%20The%20amount%20paid%20alone%20does%20not%20explain%20the%20outcome%3A%20the%20suggested%20rule%20%60paymentAmount%3A%3Asum%20%3E%3D%2049.2%60%20only%20reaches%20a%20precision%20of%200.83.%20What%20matters%20is%20that%20the%20fine%20was%20paid%20in%20two%20steps.%20Together%20the%20three%20explanations%20cover%2065.02%20%25%20of%20the%20outcome.%20The%20remaining%203'017%20cases%20are%20not%20yet%20explained.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0Aif%20__name__%20%3D%3D%20%22__main__%22%3A%0A%20%20%20%20app.run()%0A
